predecessors.name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
predecessors.text: Greater Poland, the base of Stanisław Leszczyński's confederation ('He had earlier organized a confederation in Greater Poland'); the Warsaw confederation of January-February 1704 declared Augustus…

successors.name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
successors.text: the 1706-1708 extent of the Swedish-backed Poland, returned to the rule of Augustus II when 'Augustus II returned to the throne' after Poltava

rulers.name: Stanisław I Leszczyński
rulers.title: King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania (first reign)

ledger.x: 1704: a Swedish-backed assembly elects Stanisław Leszczyński king of Poland-Lithuania.
28 October 1704: the first dated battle of the new regime, Poniec.
1706 (Cliopatria's first shape year): the Swedish-backed Poland spreads beyond Greater Poland.
14 September 1706: Augustus II renounces the Polish throne at Altranstädt.
July 1709: Stanisław loses the throne after Poltava and Augustus returns.
8 July 1709: Stanisław's first reign ends and the Swedish-backed regime with it; he went to Swedish Pomerania and later lived at Rydzyna (page, undated).

wars.name: Swedish invasion of Poland (1701–1706)
wars.outcome: 'Swedish-led victory': the Warsaw confederation deposed Augustus in 1704, Stanisław Leszczyński was elected and, after the Swedish victories (Wschowa/Fraustadt, Toruń), Augustus renounced his claim at Altranstädt on 14 September 1706.

wars.name: Battle of Poltava
wars.outcome: Charles XII, Stanisław's main supporter, was defeated by the Russians; 'As a result, Augustus II returned to the throne' and Stanisław's first reign ended on 8 July 1709.

certainty.note: A Swedish-backed faction's holdings in a civil war; no treaty or survey line, and neither page names the extent held.
